transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... I just couldn't ignore what's happening anymore. My in-laws and I have been arguing, but I know it's not just regular family bickering. They are actually using the altar and the parish committee to push me out. They want to make everyone forget everything I have done for this family over the years. So... that's why I'm here.
How long have you believed that your in-laws and the parish committee are conspiring to push you out?

Well, it's been going on for about two months now. This whole crisis... it really started right after I had a big fight with my in-laws over the Día de los Muertos altar. That's when all of this really began.
Have you heard or seen things that other people do not hear or see?

Yes, I have. Um... on several nights, I actually heard my late mother's voice. She was telling me exactly where to put the marigolds and the candles. And... well, one time I even saw her. She was just standing right near the kitchen doorway. I told my husband she was right there, but he said no one was there. So, yes, I have been experiencing that.
Have you been feeling unusually elevated or irritable in your mood?

Yes, I have. There were days recently when I felt... well, just so bright and certain about everything. Like I had all this clarity and knew exactly what I was doing. 

But then, if anyone even questioned me about the altar, I would get so angry. I would just snap at them, almost like they were insulting my whole family. So, yes, I've definitely had moments of feeling really good and then getting very irritable.
Have you heard your mother’s voice or seen her during times when you were not feeling unusually elevated or irritable?

No, actually. The voices... and seeing my mother, that only happened during that specific time when I was barely sleeping. You know, when I was rushing around all the time, just feeling so sure that I had this special duty to fix the altar. 

Later on, when my mood dropped and I just felt so guilty and sad... I wasn't hearing or seeing those things anymore. It was really just during that time when I felt so sped up and certain.
How long did that unusually elevated or irritable mood last?

I'm not exactly sure. Um... it's hard to say because time gets a little blurry when I'm rushing around like that. I just know it went on for a while before I crashed and started feeling sad again. But as for exactly how long it lasted... I really couldn't tell you.
Would you say that period of unusually elevated or irritable mood lasted at least one week?

I really couldn't tell you if it was a full week. It might have been, but... well, like I said, I just wasn't keeping track of the days. It all felt like one long, continuous stretch of rushing around, so I don't want to just say yes and give you the wrong answer. I'm honestly not sure.
During that sped-up period, did your mood and behavior cause major problems in your ability to work, manage daily responsibilities, or get along with others?

Yes, it really did. I... well, I stopped being able to keep up with the parish preparations. My family actually had to step in and take over all my tasks for the festival. And even just at home, I wasn't managing the house the way I usually do. My husband started staying close by to watch over me, because I was missing meals and... just completely forgetting my normal routines. I really wasn't taking care of myself reliably during that time.
Did you need to be hospitalized because of this sped-up, unusually elevated or irritable period?
No, I wasn't hospitalized. My husband and my family just sort of... kept a very close eye on me at home until it passed. But I didn't go to a hospital.
Can you recall whether that continuously sped-up and unusually elevated or irritable period lasted for seven consecutive days or longer?

Like I mentioned just a bit ago, I really can't say for sure if it was seven days in a row. It's just all a blur of rushing around and not keeping track of time. I don't want to guess and tell you the wrong thing, so I honestly just don't know.
Could your husband or family estimate how many consecutive days that sped-up, unusually elevated or irritable period lasted?

I haven't really asked them about the exact number of days. They just told me it felt like it went on for a while, but I don't know if they were counting the days either. I could ask my husband later if you need to know for sure.
What date did the sped-up period begin, and what date did it end?
I really don't know the dates. Like I said, that whole time is just a blur to me. I wasn't looking at a calendar or keeping track of when it started or stopped.
Can your husband estimate whether that sped-up, unusually elevated or irritable period lasted seven consecutive days or longer?

I'm really just not sure. Like I was saying a minute ago, I haven't asked him about a specific number of days. He might be able to give you a better guess if you talked to him, but... well, right now I just don't know what his answer would be.
During that sped-up period, when you slept very little, did you still feel rested and have plenty of energy the next day?

I'm not really sure about that. Like I said before, that whole time is just a big blur to me. I know I wasn't sleeping much, but... I honestly don't remember if I woke up feeling rested or if I had a lot of energy. I just can't recall exactly how I felt day to day back then.
Based on what your husband or family observed, was there a continuous period of at least seven days when you were clearly in that sped-up, unusually elevated or irritable state?

I really couldn't tell you for sure. I know you're trying to pin down exactly how long it lasted, but I just haven't had that specific conversation with my husband or my family. They definitely noticed I was off, but whether it was exactly seven days in a row... I just don't know what they'd say. You'd probably have to ask them to get a real answer on the timeline.
From your husband’s or family’s observations, was there a continuous period of at least seven days when you were unusually elevated or irritable and noticeably sped up?

I think... well, didn't you just ask me that? I really don't have a different answer for you. Like I just said, I don't know if they saw it happening for seven days straight. We haven't talked about the exact number of days. If you need to know their side of the timeline, you'll really just have to bring my husband in and ask him.
During the period when you heard your mother’s voice and saw her, were you also continuously more energized or unusually irritable than usual?

Yes, that's exactly when it was. Hearing her voice and seeing her... that really only happened during that time when I was barely sleeping and just rushing around everywhere. That was when I was so sure I had a special duty to fix the altar. 

Later on, when my mood dropped, I still felt awful—just really guilty and sad—but I wasn't hearing or seeing those things anymore. It was only during that sped-up time.
Based on your husband’s observations, did your unusually elevated or irritable, sped-up state last continuously for at least seven consecutive days?

Doctor, I feel like we're going in circles here. You've asked me this a few times now, and my answer hasn't changed. I really don't know exactly how many days my husband thought it lasted. We haven't sat down and counted the days. Like I said before, you'll have to ask him if you need to know exactly how long he thought it went on for.
Can you identify any uninterrupted stretch of seven consecutive days during which you remained unusually elevated or irritable and sped up?

Doctor, I... I really don't know how else to say it. You keep asking me about this seven-day thing, and I just don't have a clear answer for you. I was so caught up in what I was doing, with the altar and my mother's voice, that I wasn't marking off days on a calendar. It was a blur. So, no, I can't sit here and swear to you that it was exactly seven uninterrupted days. I just know it happened.
Would you be willing for me to ask your husband how many consecutive days he observed you in that sped-up, unusually elevated or irritable state?

Yes, that's fine. I think it would probably be helpful for you to talk to him. He was the one watching it all happen, so he'd definitely have a better idea of how many days it lasted than I do. You can go ahead and ask him.
